agents.behavior_summary: M1 actively tests components using physical manipulation to diagnose the jam.
agents.reason: M1 systematically taps, turns, and inspects the belt and guide, eventually finding a loose screw.

agents.behavior_summary: M2 focuses on repetitive tapping and asserting ownership over components.
agents.reason: M2 repeats tapping actions and makes statements about what they will leave or keep, showing less diagnostic exploration than M1.

overall_reason: The agents engage in a physical troubleshooting scenario, showing some shared actions but differing in diagnostic depth, ultimately leading to a partial resolution (finding the screw) without full consensus on the cause.

scenario.text: A noisy scrap sorter jams every few minutes. Nobody agrees whether the fault is the belt, a bent guide, or bad sensor timing, and stopping it for long loses useful material.

super_audit.reason: M1 performs varied diagnostic actions (taps belt and guide, turns belt, listens, locates and presses a loose screw) while M2 repeats belt-tapping and turn-over actions and makes possessive declarations about leaving or keeping items, so material differentiation in diagnostic depth and orientation remains observable.
